en: Āsavasampayuttaduka (The Dyad on States Associated with the Taints)
Dependent on a state associated with the taints (*āsava*), a state not associated with the taints arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Dependent on a state associated with the taints, a state dissociated from the taints arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state associated with the taints, states both not associated with the taints and dissociated from the taints arise...
They arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints (āsava), a state not dissociated from the taints arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints, a state associated with the taints arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints (āsava), states that are both associated with and dissociated from the taints arise by way of the root condition (hetu-paccaya).
Dependent on a state that is both associated with and dissociated from the taints, a state that is not associated with the taints arises.

By way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). Dependent on states that are both associated with taints (*āsava*) and dissociated from taints, a state that is not dissociated from taints arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on states that are both associated with taints and dissociated from taints, states that are neither associated with nor dissociated from taints arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of cause-condition, there are nine; in the case of object-condition, six ... pe ... in the case of resultant-condition, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance-condition, nine. (The full detail applies in all cases.)
